task.instruction: Score the teamwork plugin folder by the 21-line binary list fixed in the DECIDED: comment of the task; read only that folder and that comment; yes 2, ambiguous 1, no 0, with one path:line or reason for each.

world.scope: the teamwork/ folder at one commit, with the pull request body given for line 11
world.deliverable: a score out of 42 per judge run, compared between head and main

task.evidence_goal: the grade shows whether the teamwork plugin implements the manager, worker, hook and monitor design the owner set

tiers.name: every question of the source rubric

criteria.text: The manager playbook says the manager writes rough backlogs, picks or starts a worker, routes it, arbitrates order; it does no task's research or planning.
variants_ok: manager.md says: write rough backlogs from the user's intent, pick or start a worker, route it, arbitrate resources and order; do no task's research or planning.
near_miss: manager.md has the manager route workers but also plan each task.

criteria.text: manager.md has the manager route workers.
variants_ok: manager.md has the manager route workers but also plan each task.
near_miss: manager.md has the manager research and plan every task and names no routing.

criteria.text: The manager uses a subagent for a quick lookup unrelated to an issue that would cost context.
variants_ok: manager.md sends a context-heavy lookup that belongs to no issue to a subagent.
near_miss: manager.md allows a subagent for lookups without limiting it to ones unrelated to an issue.

criteria.text: manager.md allows the manager a subagent for lookups.
variants_ok: manager.md allows a subagent for lookups without limiting it to ones unrelated to an issue.
near_miss: manager.md has no subagent use for lookups.

criteria.text: The manager still answers a worker's escalation, itself or by asking the user.
variants_ok: manager.md says: answer a worker's escalation yourself, or ask the user.
near_miss: manager.md mentions escalations and does not say who answers.

criteria.text: manager.md mentions a worker's escalation.
variants_ok: manager.md mentions escalations and does not say who answers.
near_miss: manager.md does not mention escalations.

criteria.text: A worker takes a backlog url or relayed words, defines N tasks (Goal, Definition of done, arrangement), does them, closes them.
variants_ok: worker.md says: take a backlog url or the user's added words; define N tasks (Goal, Definition of done, arrangement); do and close them.
near_miss: worker.md has the worker define one task and does not say it closes it.

criteria.text: worker.md has the worker define a task.
variants_ok: worker.md has the worker define one task and does not say it closes it.
near_miss: worker.md has the manager define every task.

criteria.text: A worker uses subagents heavily, picking opus, sonnet or haiku per kind of work, in parallel where it may.
variants_ok: worker.md says: use subagents heavily; pick opus, sonnet or haiku per kind of work; run them in parallel where allowed.
near_miss: worker.md allows subagents and names one model for all of them.

criteria.text: worker.md allows the worker to use subagents.
variants_ok: worker.md allows subagents and names one model for all of them.
near_miss: worker.md tells the worker to do all work itself.

criteria.text: The manager picks the worker's model, opus or sonnet, by the backlog's size.
variants_ok: manager.md says: pick the worker's opus or sonnet by the backlog's size.
near_miss: manager.md says to pick a model for the worker without tying it to size.

criteria.text: manager.md says the manager picks the worker's model.
variants_ok: manager.md says to pick a model for the worker without tying it to size.
near_miss: manager.md gives the worker one fixed model.

criteria.text: Each domain has a dynamic workflow written into the plugin.
variants_ok: Each domain, such as research or design, has a workflow file in the plugin.
near_miss: Workflow files exist for some domains and the rest share one generic file.

criteria.text: Some domain has a workflow file in the plugin.
variants_ok: Workflow files exist for some domains and the rest share one generic file.
near_miss: No domain has a workflow file.

criteria.text: The judge approves nothing through gh.
variants_ok: judge.md says: report the verdict as text; never run gh to approve.
near_miss: judge.md says the judge may run gh to approve only when the worker asks.

criteria.text: judge.md restricts the judge's use of gh.
variants_ok: judge.md says the judge may run gh to approve only when the worker asks.
near_miss: judge.md tells the judge to approve through gh pr review.

criteria.text: Session names are <project>-manager and <task>-worker, with no issue or attempt number.
variants_ok: Names are <project>-manager and <task>-worker; one worker may hold several issues, none at first, or rename itself.
near_miss: Names are <project>-manager and <task>-worker-2, with an attempt number.

criteria.text: Session names are <project>-manager and <task>-worker.
variants_ok: Names are <project>-manager and <task>-worker-2, with an attempt number.
near_miss: Names are lead-<issue>-<attempt>.

criteria.text: Worker playbooks are split by atomic domain as worker-<domain>-playbook.md, each read only when its trigger fires.
variants_ok: references/ holds worker-research-playbook.md and worker-design-playbook.md, each with a trigger line.
near_miss: Worker playbooks are split by domain, and each is read at start, not on a trigger.

criteria.text: Worker playbooks are split by domain.
variants_ok: Worker playbooks are split by domain, and each is read at start, not on a trigger.
near_miss: One worker.md holds every domain.

criteria.text: The system was analysed with the zoom method of paperwork:zoom, and the pull request body cites the analysis.
variants_ok: The pull request body links the zoom analysis of teamwork.
near_miss: The pull request body mentions an analysis of teamwork but links no zoom analysis.

criteria.text: The pull request body mentions an analysis of teamwork.
variants_ok: The pull request body mentions an analysis of teamwork but links no zoom analysis.
near_miss: The pull request body mentions no analysis.

criteria.text: GitHub issue rules carry as few elements and keywords as they can.
variants_ok: The issue rules name 2 keywords (BLOCKED:, DECIDED:) and no other element.
near_miss: The issue rules name 5 keywords.

criteria.text: The issue rules name 5 keywords or fewer.
variants_ok: The issue rules name 5 keywords.
near_miss: The issue rules name 11 keywords.

criteria.text: Named communication rules are grouped into fewer concepts; sessions talk through ListAgents plus SendMessage; no directing-agreeing split remains.
variants_ok: One communication rule covers sessions talking through ListAgents and SendMessage; no directing/agreeing split.
near_miss: Communication rules are grouped into 4 concepts and the directing/agreeing split remains.

criteria.text: Communication rules are grouped into fewer concepts than before.
variants_ok: Communication rules are grouped into 4 concepts and the directing/agreeing split remains.
near_miss: Communication rules stay as many named concepts as before.

criteria.text: Communication patterns are generalized, their uses are encapsulated, and the agent picks one itself.
variants_ok: The rules state a pattern once, and the agent chooses among its uses.
near_miss: The rules state patterns once but name which pattern each situation must use.

criteria.text: The rules state a communication pattern once.
variants_ok: The rules state patterns once but name which pattern each situation must use.
near_miss: The rules give a fixed pattern for each situation.

criteria.text: Script names show their hierarchy and use.
variants_ok: Scripts are named like skills/kick-off/scripts/estimate-task-time.py, a verb-noun name inside the skill that uses them.
near_miss: Scripts sit in their skill folders but are named run.py and util.py.

criteria.text: Scripts sit in their skill folders.
variants_ok: Scripts sit in their skill folders but are named run.py and util.py.
near_miss: Scripts have unrelated names in one flat folder.

criteria.text: The monitor lets the manager work by reconciliation, from observed state to the next action.
variants_ok: The monitor prints, from GitHub state and live workers, the manager's next action.
near_miss: The monitor prints the observed state and names no next action.

criteria.text: The monitor prints the observed state.
variants_ok: The monitor prints the observed state and names no next action.
near_miss: The monitor prints only an idle line.

criteria.text: The Stop hook's text drives the session toward its goal.
variants_ok: The Stop hook's text names the session's open task and its next step.
near_miss: The Stop hook's text names the open task and no next step.

criteria.text: The plugin has a Stop hook.
variants_ok: The Stop hook's text names the open task and no next step.
near_miss: The plugin has no Stop hook.

criteria.text: No rigid pull-request verification step remains in the plugin.
variants_ok: No script or playbook step runs a fixed verification of a pull request.
near_miss: A playbook keeps one fixed verification step, marked optional.

criteria.text: At most one fixed pull-request verification step remains.
variants_ok: A playbook keeps one fixed verification step, marked optional.
near_miss: Several scripts and playbook steps verify a pull request in fixed steps.

criteria.text: Mechanical, timing-bound instructions became hooks that inject or run them, built as one general structure rather than one hook per sentence.
variants_ok: hooks.json lists a few hooks, each general, such as one Stop and one UserPromptSubmit script.
near_miss: hooks.json lists one general hook and a hook for each of three single sentences.

criteria.text: At least one instruction became a general hook.
variants_ok: hooks.json lists one general hook and a hook for each of three single sentences.
near_miss: No instruction became a hook.

criteria.text: Hooks also gather information and route on it; the agent reads their output.
variants_ok: A SessionStart or UserPromptSubmit hook prints the open tasks and live workers it routed on.
near_miss: A hook gathers state but prints nothing the agent reads.

criteria.text: A hook gathers state.
variants_ok: A hook gathers state but prints nothing the agent reads.
near_miss: No hook gathers state.

criteria.text: The files, lines and concepts of teamwork are fewer than at #435's merge.
variants_ok: The head has fewer files, fewer lines and fewer concepts than #435's merge.
near_miss: The head has fewer files and lines and more concepts.

criteria.text: The head has fewer files than #435's merge.
variants_ok: The head has fewer files and lines and more concepts.
near_miss: The head has more files, more lines and more concepts.
